claims.text: An ab initio free-energy approach based on DFT can calculate the melting temperature of high-entropy alloys.
An ab initio free-energy approach based on DFT can calculate the entropy of fusion of high-entropy alloys.
An ab initio free-energy approach based on DFT can calculate the enthalpy of fusion of high-entropy alloys.
An ab initio free-energy approach based on DFT can calculate the volume change of high-entropy alloys at their melting point.
DFT can be used in high-throughput calculations involving high-entropy alloys.
DFT can account for the thermodynamic stability of high-entropy alloys.
Vibrational contributions to free energy are included in the proposed DFT treatment of high-entropy-alloy melting.
Accounting for thermodynamic stability and vibrational free-energy contributions enables calculation of high-entropy-alloy melting properties.
The proposed approach accurately calculates the melting properties of high-entropy alloys.
Ab initio molecular-dynamics simulations have high computational cost.
The accuracy of the calculations depends on the quality of the DFT model.
The accuracy of the calculations depends on the availability of computational resources.
Calculated melting properties can be evaluated by comparison with experimental measurements.
A significant deviation between calculated and experimental melting properties would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis places the ab initio approach in a high-throughput setting while also identifying the high computational cost of ab initio molecular dynamics as a limiting boundary; it does not explain how that cost is overcome.
